reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates that a hot-press sintered Hf coating on a VZrHfNbTa alloy forms a dense HfO2 scale that reduces oxidation and surface degradation at high temperature. However, the evidence is for oxidation resistance in air, not corrosion resistance in molten aluminum, so the key premise that this HfO2 barrier prevents molten-aluminum corrosion is not directly supported.
premises: Hafnium coating can be densified on a substrate via hot-press sintering
Hafnium coating forms a dense, protective HfO2 scale at high temperature in oxidizing environment
HfO2 scale prevents surface degradation (pulverization, dents) of the underlying material
HfO2 scale acts as a barrier against chemical attack/diffusion
The protective effect is demonstrated for a refractory high-entropy alloy containing boride-forming elements (V, Zr, Hf, Nb, Ta)
